items.followUp: How is cobalt-60 used in the treatment of cancer?

rubric.why: Identifies the radioactive isotope used in cancer treatment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming cobalt-60 or Co-60.

rubric.why: Explains how the isotope's radiation acts against cancer.
rubric.description: States that gamma rays are directed at cancer cells to destroy or kill them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing gamma rays destroying or killing cancer cells.

modelAnswer: Cobalt-60 is used in the treatment of cancer because it emits gamma rays.
The gamma rays are directed at cancer cells to destroy them.
